strings.title: Cargo That Never Left
strings.hint: Start with the engraved identifier, then add seal and weight. Who connects the holding order, the exception and the private collection destination?
strings.solvedText: Mays Fadel arranged the attempted diversion. Label 91 moved to light case K14; label 18 moved to K41, which still held A-04 under seal 718. The case does not rest on a filmed hand: her K41 holding order, approval of 26 kg despite a prior successful calibration, J6 directed to her private unit and search for another vehicle before the alarm converge on intent and control. Mere access does not implicate Haroun, Laith or Sahar. The prototype never left; it was recovered in the holding enclosure at 18:40.
strings.summary.text: A sealed case reached the research centre without the Horizon scanning head. There was no opening in transit and no duplicate prototype. Distinguish the permanent case identity, its seal and its removable destination label. Identify who attempted to divert the shipment and where the prototype was when movements stopped.
strings.summary.victim.name: Al-Madar Marine Research Institute
strings.summary.victim.note: The only working prototype; no human casualties.
strings.scene.address: Al-Madar Institute — shipping station and inner harbour
strings.scene.intro: A floor scale, one loading lane and a guarded returns enclosure. Case identifiers are fixed to the metal shells; destination labels hang outside and can be moved. The movements listed in this file are covered by continuous footage.
strings.scene.notes[0]: Seals secure the lids; moving a destination label does not break a seal.
strings.scene.notes[1]: All case movements were stopped after the report.
strings.scene.notes[2]: All times use the same calibrated station clock.
strings.evidence[0].title: Packing record and photograph
strings.evidence[0].desc: 16:50: A-04 was inside K41, seal 718, destination label 91. K14 contained empty brackets, seal 719, label 18. Nada and Laith signed the record. There is no second prototype.
strings.evidence[1].title: Weight and calibration log
strings.evidence[1].desc:
17:12 — K41: 146 kg.
17:14 — K14: 26 kg.
17:31 — K14 / label 91: 26 kg; Fawzi objected.
17:33 — Calibration passed. No fault recorded.
strings.evidence[2].title: Two labels at the gate
strings.evidence[2].desc: Original 17:25 photograph: K41 / 718 / 91 and K14 / 719 / 18. All four suspects could access the loading area afterwards; the camera did not capture a hand moving a label.
strings.evidence[3].title: Departure recording
strings.evidence[3].desc: 17:36: The vehicle’s only load was K14, bearing label 91 and seal 719. Its engraved identifier is readable. K41 was not in the vehicle.
strings.evidence[4].title: Internal holding instruction
strings.evidence[4].desc: 17:30: Haroun moved K41 with label 18 into the returns enclosure for J6 under an original order signed by Mays. Seal 718 remained intact and the case stayed within the guarded perimeter until inventory.
strings.evidence[5].title: Shipment weight exception
strings.evidence[5].desc: 17:34: Mays’s original signature approved label 91 at 26 instead of 146, citing “scale failure”. Footage shows her signing in Haroun’s presence. The reverse carries the successful calibration result entered before signature.
strings.evidence[6].title: Returns request J6
strings.evidence[6].desc: Issued 17:22: collection of label 18 at 20:00 in Al-Jisr’s name, “worthless packaging, 26 kg”. Mays arranged the appointment by phone. At issue, 18 was on K14; the request alone cannot prove what she later intended to load.
strings.evidence[7].title: Collection address and messages
strings.evidence[7].desc: The J6 destination is a private unit rented by Mays, not Al-Jisr’s warehouse. The company exists but denied booking J6 and refused collection away from its premises. Authenticated messages predating the alarm show Mays proposing another vehicle after cancellation.
strings.suspects[0].name: Mays Fadel
strings.suspects[0].relation: Controls movements and exceptions; has debts and a private business.
strings.suspects[0].statement: I opened no case. Haroun moved them; Laith knows the prototype. I signed the weight exception after being told the scale was faulty. J6 is routine. Having a key to a private unit does not prove theft.
strings.suspects[1].name: Haroun Shawqi
strings.suspects[1].relation: Denied a permanent job; received money from a second-hand dealer.
strings.suspects[1].alibi: Moved cases under orders and stopped at the weight discrepancy.
strings.suspects[1].statement: I recorded the engraved number, not the label colour. Fawzi objected to 26 instead of 146, so I waited for Mays to sign. The payment was for my children’s bicycle; the advertisement and receipt are available.
strings.suspects[2].name: Laith Adel
strings.suspects[2].relation: Design-credit dispute and a competitor’s job offer.
strings.suspects[2].alibi: Packed the prototype in Nada’s presence and remained at the station.
strings.suspects[2].statement: I copied drawings without permission to document my contribution, but did not move the head. I photographed A-04 before closing the case. I cannot approve a weight exception or a returns order.
strings.suspects[3].name: Sahar Mounir
strings.suspects[3].relation: Fleet debts and a recent insurance increase.
strings.suspects[3].alibi: Continuous journey from 17:36 to 18:05 with no stops.
strings.suspects[3].statement: I signed for route label 91, not the contents of the case. I asked about the exception and was told it was approved. I never opened the lid and delivered seal 719 intact.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Nada Youssef
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I placed 91 on K41 and 18 on K14. The 17:25 photograph shows both engraved identifiers, labels and seals. I saw A-04 packed in K41 and observed no later transfer between the cases.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Fawzi Nader
strings.witnesses[1].statement: At 17:31 K14 carried label 91 and weighed 26 kg. I recorded an objection because 146 was expected. The scale passed its 17:33 calibration check, which I wrote on the reverse of the exception before it was signed.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Iman Fawzi
strings.witnesses[2].statement: K14 arrived with seal 719 intact. We filmed its opening and found empty brackets. I reported the discrepancy before moving anything; the engraved identifier is visible in the footage.
strings.folders[0].name: Packing list
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: 31-D1 — Packing list
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body:
K41 — A-04 — 146 kg — seal 718 — label 91 — research centre.
K14 — empty brackets — 26 kg — seal 719 — label 18 — returns.
Nada and Laith verified the engraved identifiers. A label is not a case identifier.
strings.folders[1].name: Continuous journey
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: 31-D2 — Continuous journey
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Cameras and the route log cover 17:36–18:05. There were no stops or access to the load; seal 719 was unbroken. This excludes an in-transit contents swap, but does not establish that the correct case was loaded.
strings.folders[2].name: Mays’s response to the records
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: 31-D3 — Mays’s response to the records
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: Mays says she signed without reading and Haroun switched papers on her desk. She describes her private unit as scrap storage for a staff fund. The institute issued no authorisation for this activity. Footage establishes her signature, but does not show the label swap.
strings.folders[3].name: Loading-area access
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: 31-D4 — Loading-area access
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: Mays, Haroun, Laith and Sahar all passed through after 17:25. No replacement labels were issued. Access alone does not identify the offender; compare the original instructions, weight and returns destination.
strings.folders[4].name: Three separate suspicions
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: 31-D5 — Three separate suspicions
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: Haroun’s payment matches a bicycle advertisement and earlier receipt. Laith copied drawings without permission, with no evidence that he moved the prototype. Sahar’s insurance increase covered the entire fleet a week earlier. These facts do not establish a joint conspiracy.
strings.folders[5].name: The 18:40 inventory
strings.folders[5].docs[0].title: 31-D6 — The 18:40 inventory
strings.folders[5].docs[0].body: In the holding enclosure: K41 / label 18 / intact seal 718. Opened before Nada and police: A-04 was inside, total weight 146 kg. Recovery was recorded inside the station before any returns collection.
strings.reports[0].title: 31-R1 — Seal and identifier examination
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation and examination team
strings.reports[0].body: The seals were original and intact until documented opening. An external label can move without opening a lid. There is no evidence of cut seals, a second prototype or an unrecorded vehicle. Engraved identifiers were unchanged.
strings.reports[1].title: 31-R2 — Scope of the incident
strings.reports[1].author: Investigation and examination team
strings.reports[1].body: All orders were halted on the report. The institute authorised neither sale of A-04 nor delivery to a private unit. The prototype did not leave, no sale was completed and no accomplice is established. Distinguish attempted diversion from successful removal.
